extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and Technology Center Directors (Patent Examining Corps)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examiners on when to make 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph (indefiniteness) rejections for means (or step) plus function claim limitations that invoke 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph, including required analysis, disclosure checks, linkage requirements, and form paragraphs to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: 3-prong analysis for presuming invocation of 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim limitation is presumed to invoke 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph, if it meets the 3-prong analysis set forth in MPEP 2181, subsection I.: (1) The claim limitation must use the phrase “means for” or “step for”; (2) The phrase “means for” or “step for” recited in the claim must be modified by functional language; and (3) The phrase “means for” or “step for” recited in the claim must not be modified by sufficient structure, material, or acts for achieving the specified function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this 3-prong test as the starting presumption. If the claim meets all three prongs, treat it as a means/step-plus-function limitation under 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph. See MPEP 2181 for examples and further analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear whether limitation invokes 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph (phrase used but sufficiency of recited structure unclear)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the phrase “means for” or “step for” is used and the claim is modified by some structure, material, or acts, it may be unclear whether the recited structure, material, or acts are sufficient for performing the claimed function and thus whether 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unclear to one of ordinary skill in the art whether the recited structure/material/acts are sufficient to perform the claimed function, a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph may be appropriate. Examiners may use form paragraph ¶ 7.34.16. Require applicant to amend the claim to clarify whether it should be treated as means-plus-function (e.g., delete or modify “means for”/“step for”) or otherwise clarify sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unclear whether limitation invokes 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph (phrase not used)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claim limitation does not include the phrase “means for” or “step for”, it will not be presumed to invoke 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph. However, if the limitation is written as a function to be performed and does not recite sufficient structure, material, or acts, 112, sixth paragraph might apply; if it is unclear whether it does, a 112, second paragraph rejection may be appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unclear whether the limitation invokes 112, sixth paragraph, examiner may require applicant to either (a) amend the claim to include the phrase “means for” or “step for” in accordance with the 3-prong analysis, or (b) show that the limitation lacks sufficient structure and thus should be treated as function-only. Examiners may use form paragraph ¶ 7.34.17 and must precede it with form paragraphs 7.30.02 and 7.34.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: No disclosure or insufficient disclosure of corresponding structure/material/acts in the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a limitation is determined to be a means (or step) plus function limitation invoking 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph, the written description must disclose the corresponding structure, material, or acts that perform the claimed function (as viewed by one skilled in the art). A rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph is appropriate if there is no disclosure or insufficient disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the specification (including drawings, figures, tables, sequence listings) to identify corresponding structure; disclosure only by incorporation-by-reference is insufficient. A bare statement that known techniques can be used is insufficient. Examiners may use form paragraph ¶ 7.34.18. Applicant may be required to (a) amend the claim to avoid means-plus-function, or (b) amend the written description to expressly recite the corresponding structure/material/acts without introducing new matter, or (c) state on the record where the corresponding structure is implicitly disclosed (with reference to 37 CFR 1.75(d) and MPEP 2181/608.01(o)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer-implemented means-plus-function claims require disclosure of an algorithm (corresponding structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: For computer-implemented means-plus-function limitations, the corresponding structure must be more than a general purpose computer or microprocessor; it must include the algorithm that transforms the general purpose computer into a special-purpose computer that performs the function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written description must disclose the algorithm (may be expressed as math, prose, flow chart, etc.). Mere reference to a general purpose computer with appropriate programming or merely reciting 'software' without detail is insufficient. A 112, second paragraph rejection is appropriate if no corresponding algorithm is disclosed. See cited Federal Circuit decisions (e.g., Aristocrat, WMS, Finisar) and MPEP 2181 for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for written description and enablement under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph when structure is insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no or insufficient disclosure of the corresponding structure, examiner should determine whether the written description and enablement requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph are met for the claim as construed (including the full scope of corresponding structure and equivalents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To satisfy written description, the specification must describe the invention in sufficient detail that one skilled in the art can reasonably conclude the inventor had possession. For enablement, the specification must enable the full scope claimed; if more than routine experimentation would be required (e.g., to generate a missing program/algorithm), an enablement rejection under 112, first paragraph may be warranted. Use MPEP 2164.06(c), 2181, and cited cases for guidance and examples (e.g., mechanical vs electronic sensors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to clearly link or associate disclosed structure/material/acts to the claimed function
rubrics_metrics.description: The structure disclosed in the written description qualifies as the corresponding structure only if the specification or prosecution history clearly links or associates that structure to the function recited in the means-plus-function limitation. If one of ordinary skill cannot identify what structure performs the claimed function, a 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph rejection is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may use form paragraph ¶ 7.34.19. Applicant may be required to (a) amend the claim to avoid means-plus-function treatment, (b) amend the written description to clearly link the structure to the function without new matter, or (c) state on the record where the corresponding structure is set forth. The 'clear link' requirement is the quid pro quo for employing 112, sixth paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit or inherent disclosure: acceptable only if one skilled in the art can identify corresponding structure; require clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: In rare circumstances where the specification implicitly (rather than expressly) sets forth the structure/material/acts that perform the claimed function, 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph may be satisfied if one skilled in the art can identify that structure. However, the record must be clarified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When disclosure is only implicit/inherent, the examiner should require applicant to either (a) amend the written description to expressly recite the corresponding structure/material/acts and clearly link them to the claimed function (without new matter), or (b) state on the record what the corresponding structure/material/acts are. Examiners may use form paragraph ¶ 7.34.20 and may alternatively state on the record what structure is implicitly set forth. Cite 37 CFR 1.75(d) and MPEP 608.01(o).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural/form paragraph usage and examiner notes
rubrics_metrics.description: When issuing 112, second paragraph rejections in these contexts, examiners should use the provided form paragraphs (¶ 7.34.16–¶ 7.34.20) and follow the specified bracketed insertion and preceding-paragraph requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each form paragraph contains bracketed fields to recite the claim element and explain the deficiency; form paragraphs ¶ 7.34.16–¶ 7.34.19 must be preceded by form paragraphs 7.30.02 and 7.34.01. Examiners should follow the Examiner Notes in each form paragraph (e.g., what to include in each bracket) and cite relevant MPEP sections and case law where appropriate.
